definitions.Parties: The two or more parties who signed the contract
definitions.Effective Date: The date when the contract is effective
definitions.Expiration Date: On what date will the contract's initial term expire?
definitions.Renewal Term: What is the renewal term after the initial term expires? This includes automatic extensions and unilateral extensions with prior notice.
definitions.Notice Period To Terminate Renewal: What is the notice period required to terminate renewal?
definitions.Governing Law: Which state/country's law governs the interpretation of the contract?
definitions.Termination For Convenience: Can a party terminate this contract without cause (solely by giving a notice and allowing a waiting period to expire)?
definitions.Anti-Assignment: Is consent or notice required of a party if the contract is assigned to a third party?
definitions.Change Of Control: Does one party have the right to terminate or is consent or notice required of the counterparty if such party undergoes a change of control, such as a merger, stock sale, transfer of all or substantially all of its assets or business, or assignment by operation of law?
definitions.Cap On Liability: Does the contract include a cap on liability upon the breach of a party’s obligation? This includes time limitation for the counterparty to bring claims or maximum amount for recovery.
definitions.Uncapped Liability: Is a party’s liability uncapped upon the breach of its obligation in the contract? This also includes uncap liability for a particular type of breach such as IP infringement or breach of confidentiality obligation.
definitions.Minimum Commitment: Is there a minimum order size or minimum amount or units per-time period that one party must buy from the counterparty under the contract?
definitions.Exclusivity: Is there an exclusive dealing commitment with the counterparty? This includes a commitment to procure all “requirements” from one party of certain technology, goods, or services or a prohibition on licensing or selling technology, goods or services to third parties, or a prohibition on collaborating or working with other parties), whether during the contract or after the contract ends (or both).
definitions.Audit Rights: Does a party have the right to audit the books, records, or physical locations of the counterparty to ensure compliance with the contract?
definitions.Insurance: Is there a requirement for insurance that must be maintained by one party for the benefit of the counterparty?
definitions.Post-Termination Services: Is a party subject to obligations after the termination or expiration of a contract, including any post-termination transition, payment, transfer of IP, wind-down, last-buy, or similar commitments?
definitions.Non-Compete: Is there a restriction on the ability of a party to compete with the counterparty or operate in a certain geography or business or technology sector?
